likelyCauses: iOS renderer (Kuikly/RN side) applies a different word/breakpoint strategy for inline code spans, failing to break at segment separators the way Android does.
Task-chip token regex / known-ref gate on iOS rejects bare '#42' and '#43' because they are not in the loaded entity set, while Android tags every bare #number regardless of resolution.
Text-measuring / layout engine on iOS measures inline code as a single long token and refuses mid-token breaks that Android performs at '/' or '-' boundaries.
suggestedFixes: Unify inline-code wrapping logic so both platforms break long paths/commands at the same boundaries (e.g., segment separators) and produce matching line counts.
Decide explicitly whether bare #numbers should be task chips on iOS (currently treated as plain text) and align behavior with the intentional Android tag-everything policy.
Re-run the long-inline-code Slock test on iOS after the wrap/break change and verify the long-path and long-command blocks match Android's line-break positions exactly.
intentional: Bare '#520' and any other unknown-ref bare #number task chips: Android tags them as task chips; iOS renders them as plain text. Per artin's ruling (task #416), Android's tag-everything behavior is the kept platform behavior.
